scope: Raw Annex B HEVC input decoded and re-encoded to VP8 and VP9 WebM without Docker.
commands: ffmpeg -ss 0 -t 4 -i test.mkv -map 0:v:0 -an -c:v copy -bsf:v hevc_mp4toannexb -f hevc work/hevc-webm-feasibility/source.hevc
ffmpeg -framerate 24 -i source.hevc -an -vf scale='min(640,iw)':-2 -c:v libvpx -deadline realtime -cpu-used 8 -lag-in-frames 0 -auto-alt-ref 0 -b:v 600k -threads 4 -slices 4 -f webm vp8.webm

ffmpeg -framerate 24 -i source.hevc -an -vf scale='min(640,iw)':-2 -c:v libvpx-vp9 -deadline realtime -cpu-used 8 -lag-in-frames 0 -auto-alt-ref 0 -row-mt 1 -tile-columns 1 -b:v 600k -threads 4 -f webm vp9.webm
interpretation: Both outputs are genuine lossy codec conversions; FFprobe identified VP8 and VP9 and FFmpeg decoded every output frame.
Raw HEVC cannot be losslessly wrapped when B-frame presentation timestamps are absent, but genuine re-encoding can synthesize timing under the already-disclosed elementary-stream policy.
The browser routes remain non-public until rebuilt Wasm, three-run complete-Chromium memory, repeatability, validation, cancellation, write-failure, privacy, and cleanup gates pass.

cleanup.policy: Deleted after compact evidence was recorded; no converted media is retained.
